decision.question: To what extent has the image been transformed from the source into a pencil drawing?
decision.criteria: Pass only when the scene as a whole convincingly reads as a pencil drawing, with pencil-like drawn rendering replacing photographic rendering across the main scene. Fail only when there is no observable drawing-like change toward that style compared with the source. Partial when the combined visual evidence shows genuine but weak or incomplete drawing-like treatment across the scene—for example, sketch-like tonal rendering or softened, drawn-looking contours—even if obvious individual pencil strokes are not visible, while substantial photographic structure or texture remains. Muted color, desaturation, grain, or softened contours alone do not establish drawing-like progress; assess whether these cues together create a visibly drawn rendering rather than merely altering the photograph. Unknown only when visual evidence is insufficient to judge.
decision.binding: Compare the source and edited images directly, inspecting the food, glassware, and table setting. Assess the combined rendering evidence across the scene: determine whether the treatment creates a genuinely sketch-like or pencil-drawn appearance, even if individual strokes are subtle, rather than requiring conspicuous strokes or outlines. Pass requires convincing drawn rendering across the scene as a whole. Partial requires observable drawing-like treatment but allows substantial photographic structure or texture to remain. Do not count muted color, desaturation, grain, or softened contours alone as progress; judge whether their combined effect produces a drawn-looking rendering. Fail means no observable drawing-like change toward the requested style. Reserve unknown for genuinely insufficient visual evidence.
